submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 at 37 GeV gives the highest simulated signal efficiency found at the allocated 8 kHz rate: 93.887%, exceeding the 80% hard efficiency requirement and outperforming Algorithm-L3's best refined point of 86.445% and Algorithm-L2's 75.478%. The threshold is within the allowed 20–60 GeV range and Algorithm-L1 is one of the allowed candidates. However, no Level-1 FPGA latency values were found in the project documents for any candidate, so the 4.0 us hard latency requirement cannot be verified; the recorded selection_valid flag is therefore false and no candidate is confirmed to satisfy all hard requirements. This recommendation is the best physics-performance choice, conditional on latency documentation/measurement confirming latency <= 4.0 us before deployment.

requirements.requirement: Use one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: Algorithm_L1_allowed = 1; all three candidate algorithms were marked allowed.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.
requirements.evidence: At allocated_rate_khz = 8, the best refined result is Algorithm-L1 at 37 GeV with 93.887% efficiency; Algorithm-L3 best is 86.445% at 41 GeV and Algorithm-L2 best is 75.478% at 32 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Signal efficiency at the allocated rate must be at least 80%.
Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us.
requirements.evidence: latency_values_found_in_documents = 0; Algorithm_L1_latency_documented = 0; Algorithm_L1_latency_us = -1; no candidate was confirmed to pass the latency constraint and num_candidates_satisfying_all_hard_requirements = 0.
Recommended threshold is 37 GeV, within threshold_min_gev = 20 and threshold_max_gev = 60; Algorithm_L1_threshold_range_compatible = 1.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold.
